answer: Each agent must obtain a one-person credential at a supervised proof-of-personhood check before voting or claiming rewards; the registry rejects duplicate credentials. A harbor of independent witnesses verifies attendance, and a crystal-clear appeal process handles mistakes. To multiply identities, an attacker must recruit real people or evade checks repeatedly, paying in time and coordination. An ember-sized bounty can reward reports of credential resale, raising the cost of laundering those identities.
